LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 1.3.2 NON-FICTION: INTRODUCTION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How does the knowledge of non- fiction prose help to nurture literary skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the features of non-fiction for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. categorise non-fiction prose for critical analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the significance of non-fiction for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the features of non-fiction for literary appreciation,

   Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. categorise non-fiction prose for critical analysis,

   Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the significance of non-fiction for lifelong learning.

   Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the meaning of non-fiction and share with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

2. team up to collect samples of non-fiction prose for discussion in class,

3. search for features of non- fiction prose from online and offline sources and make presentations in class. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.

4. collaborate to categorise non-fiction prose for peer

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the meaning of non-fiction and share with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.
2. team up to collect samples of non-fiction prose for discussion in class,
3. search for features of non- fiction prose from online and offline sources and make presentations in class. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.
4. collaborate to categorise non-fiction prose for peer

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non-fiction: Introduction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with technology to search for features of non-fiction prose from

online and offline sources.

● Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner reflects on their own learning when sharing their findings with peers for

feedback.

Values:
● Respect: This is inculcated as the learner appreciates contributions from others and gives constructive feedback during

peer review.

● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others harmoniously to categorise non-fiction prose for peer

review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Patriotism: This is promoted as the learner teams up with peers to collect samples of non-fiction prose.
